title.narrative: Scaling the Rainforest Value Model to Increase Community Livelihood and Preserve Rainforest of

description.narrative: West Kalimantan, Borneo is a region of extraordinary biodiversity but persistent poverty and inequality. More than 334,000 people live on monthly incomes of IDR 2.7–2.9 million, far below a living income, while social risks such as weak labor rights, child labor, and unsafe plantation work remain widespread. Livelihoods are dominated by monoculture palm oil, locking farming families into unstable earnings and hazardous conditions. At the same time, deforestation continues at scale, with more than 4.2 million hectares of rainforest cleared since 2001, including 130,000 hectares in 2024 alone. Farmers are left with an untenable choice between poverty or environmentally destructive work. This project responds by scaling Forestwise’s Rainforest Value Model, a supply chain approach that directly links farmer livelihoods with rainforest protection through co-creation with communities. At its core is the sustainable sourcing of Illipe butter, a wild-harvested forest product collected by farmers, processed locally in Sintang, and sold to global buyers under Fair for Life and organic certification. The model ensures above-market pricing, direct contracts, local value addition, and skills transfer, creating strong incentives to keep forests standing. Building on this proven value chain, the project expands into additional forest-based commodities such as natural rubber and arenga sugar, enabling income diversification and year-round cash flow.

With this project, we aim to reach beneficiaries of approximately 3,000 smallholder farmers across 100 villages, including women and indigenous communities, whose livelihoods depend on forest landscapes covering 600,000 hectares. Through participatory planning, training, and community-led monitoring, the project embeds safeguards for fair labor, gender inclusion, and child protection while reducing dependency on monoculture economies. The envisioned impact is systemic: closing living income gaps, eliminating child labor risks, strengthening local economies, and safeguarding biodiversity at landscape scale. By aligning market demand, fair pricing, and forest conservation, the Rainforest Value Model demonstrates that rainforests are more valuable intact than cleared. With SPVO’s support, this proven Theory of Change can be scaled from pilots to long-term transformation in West Kalimantan and replicated across other forest regions in Indonesia.
